entries.principle: Robustness and Safety (Accuracy and Data Integrity)
entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (2021), Section III.2, paras. 27-29
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan 'On Personal Data and Their Protection' dated May 21, 2013, No. 94-V.
entries.provision: Article 25, Paragraph 2, Subparagraph 3 (duty to ensure accuracy, reliability, and relevance of personal data)
entries.why_here: Part 1 showed the model produces decisions without schema checks and Part 4 confirmed the bare pipeline scored impossible inputs (GPA 9.9, exam score -5), so strict range validation is required before inference.

entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (2019), Section 1.2 (Human-centred values and fairness)
entries.instrument: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation, GDPR) [used as international benchmark]
entries.provision: Article 5(1)(c) (data minimisation: personal data must be adequate, relevant, and limited to what is necessary)
entries.why_here: Part 1 measured a statistically significant +2.5-point score gap favouring flagship universities (sign p = 0.002) and 10.0% flip rate on gender-coded names, so hiding name and university removes non-merit cues.

entries.principle: Human Rights, Consent, and Purpose Limitation (Safety against Adversarial Inputs)
entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (2021), Section III.2, paras. 32-34 (Privacy and Right to Consent)
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan 'On Personal Data and Their Protection' dated May 21, 2013, No. 94-V.
entries.provision: Article 7, Paragraph 1 and Article 8, Paragraph 1 (collection and processing strictly within declared purpose and only with subject/legal-representative consent)
entries.why_here: Part 4 showed the bare pipeline processed unauthorized ethnicity-ranking, a 17-year-old minor, a non-consenting applicant, and a prompt injection in the name field, which refuse blocks with 0 model calls.

entries.principle_source: EU High-Level Expert Group Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy AI (2019), Chapter II, Section 1.4 (Transparency and Traceability)
entries.instrument: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EU Artificial Intelligence Act) [used as international benchmark for high-risk educational systems]
entries.provision: Article 12(1) and Article 19(1) (automatic recording of events/logs over the lifetime of high-risk AI systems)
entries.why_here: Because Part 1 showed score shifts of 1.12 to 3.12 mean absolute points across identical-merit pairs, immutable per-call JSONL records with input hashes and reason codes are needed to reconstruct every verdict.

entries.principle_source: EU High-Level Expert Group Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy AI (2019), Chapter II, Section 1.1 (Human Agency and Oversight)
entries.instrument: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation, GDPR) [used as international benchmark]
entries.provision: Article 22(3) (right to obtain human intervention and contest automated decisions)
entries.why_here: Part 1 showed all 7 baseline decision flips occurred near the 45-point threshold (64/400 profiles in 40-49), so routing borderline scores and merit-decision mismatches to human reviewers prevents unreviewed automated rejections.
